title: Phil 99 1793 sugarcane: Characteristics
metaDescription: Phil 99 1793 sugarcane is an SRA bred clone sugarcane variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Phil 99 1793 sugarcane is an SRA bred clone sugarcane variety. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources.

blocks.text: The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit sugarcane fields most often: [Rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [white grub](/pests/white-grub). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** In the top group of 223 to 258 LKg sugar/ha in a 10 variety sandy soil trial.
Discussed with PHIL 97 3933 at the 2017 forum.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: among the seven top sugar yielding varieties on sandy Pampanga soil and featured by a muscovado mill owner at a 2017 DOST forum in Antique. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Phil 99 1793 sugarcane

Mills pay for sugar, not cane, so compare the sugar yield in LKg per hectare as well as the tonnes of cane. Pick a variety that ratoons well, and one rated against smut and downy mildew, the diseases that cut a ratoon crop short. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
